summary: TerraAnalog 3D is an interactive split-screen 3D web application that helps the public, students, and mission planners answer: "If I stand here on Earth, where am I on the Moon or Mars?" When a user selects any Earth coordinate, the system pulls 30-year climatology from the NASA POWER API and terrain elevation data, then scores it across five environmental axes against 24 benchmark sites on Mars and the Moon. The app flies a 3D planetary globe to the closest match, presenting similarity metrics, NASA orbital and rover imagery, and geological insights—making real terrestrial analog science accessible for education and mission preparation.
details:
• What it does: TerraAnalog 3D is a split-screen 3D web app where clicking any Earth coordinate pulls live NASA POWER climate and terrain data, scores it across 5 axes against 24 Mars & Moon benchmark sites, and flies a 3D planetary globe to the closest match.
  • Benefits & Impact: Turns complex terrestrial analog research into an interactive STEM tool for students, educators, and mission planners to discover Earth-to-space analogs anywhere on the globe.
  • Tech Stack: TypeScript, React 18, Three.js (@react-three/fiber), Recharts, Hono on Cloudflare Workers + D1, NASA POWER / Image Library / Mars Rover APIs, and Google Gemini.
  • Creativity & Design: Combines synchronized dual-planet 3D fly-to animations with a deterministic scoring model (math scores, AI only explains) and edge caching for sub-second repeat queries.
